question.prompt: If you walk for \(45\) minutes at a rate of \(4\) mph and then run for \(30\) minutes at a rate of \(10\) mph, how many miles have you gone at the end of one hour and \(15\) minutes?

solutions.explanation:
Because the speeds are in miles per hour, first express the times in hours. The walking time is \(45/60=3/4\) hour, and the running time is \(30/60=1/2\) hour. Distance equals speed times time, so the two distances are
\[
4\cdot\frac34=3\text{ miles},\qquad 10\cdot\frac12=5\text{ miles}.
\]
These two stages fill the entire \(75\) minutes. The total distance is \(3+5=8\) miles, choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutions.title: Convert times and add distances
